symptoms: Required, BRAIN, CodeQL, trust/security and V18 workflows were created but remained queued before runner execution.
Repository-wide Actions showed hundreds of queued runs while a smaller number of unrelated workflows were in progress.
Protected main advanced while the candidate was still awaiting exact-head execution evidence.

rootCause.primary: External GitHub Actions dispatch/capacity prevented runner assignment; queued-before-run supplied no PASS or FAIL evidence.
rootCause.secondary: Moving main invalidated the previously assumed current-main lineage before final protected merge eligibility could be proven.

recovery: Treat queued-before-run as an external execution blocker, never as code success or code failure.
Do not bypass required status checks and do not merge on stale exact-head evidence.
When current-main lineage changes under the moving-main guard, rebuild/reapply only the already validated intended diff on current protected main.
Recreate exact-head CI evidence for the new candidate and re-read protected main immediately before merge.
After merge, require exact production release.json commit_ref, context=production and concrete Netlify deploy_id before closing the obligation.

openObligation.resume: terminal exact-head gates -> immediate current-main recheck -> protected merge with expected head -> production exact-SHA/context/deploy-ID readback -> close #1510 only after proof

reuseGuidance: Future agents must search this fingerprint before diagnosing a queued release candidate. Reuse the existing moving-main and platform-capacity guards; do not invent a parallel queue, bypass required gates, or reinterpret queued state as green.
